THESE MFAs HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 01.02.2023 COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT
Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties the same is taken up for final disposal.
2. These two appeals are arising out of Judgment and award dated 03.09.2019 in MVC No.947/2017 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi.

3. While MFA No.202449/2019 is filed by the Insurance Company seeking reduction of compensation, MFA No.200477/2020 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation granted for the injury sustained in a motor vehicle accident dated 23.08.2016.
4. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

5. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that at the relevant point of time, he was working in CRPF.
On 23.08.2016, he was proceeding on motor bike bearing registration No.KA-56/E-5527 ('the Motor Cycle' for short) from Kudampur to Chincholi.

When he was near Chimmanchod Village, at about 7.00 p.m., the driver of Tum Tum bearing registration No.KA-32/C-1127 ('the offending vehicle' for short) came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
In the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in fracture.
He underwent prolonged treatment including operation.
Despite prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
After the accident, he is not able to do the work as he used to and as such, suffered loss of income.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
6. Despite due service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and as such, he was placed exparte by the Tribunal.

7. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement disputing the age, nature of the injuries Bajirao S/O Manikappa vs Sanjeevkumar And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145423741/
3 suffered and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability.

sentences.text: It is denied that after the accident, he is unable to work as he used to and as such, he has suffered loss of income.
It is a case of contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in causing the accident.
Since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, fanciful and without any basis and prays to dismiss the petition.
8. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
9. Petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and the Doctor as PW-2.

He has got marked Exs.P-1 to 16.
10.
On behalf of Respondent No.2, one witness is examined as RW-1 and Ex.R-1 is marked.

11. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.5,58,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same

The details of compensation granted are as under:

Respondent No.2 has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the compensation awarded is highly exorbitant.

Having regard to the fact that the petitioner was working at CRPF and on account of the accident,
there is no reduction in the income, the Tribunal has erred in considering loss of income and granting compensation towards future loss of income.
Petitioner has sought for voluntary retirement even before the accident.
Therefore, he is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of future income.
Consequently, the compensation granted under the head loss of future income is liable to be rejected.
Moreover, as a Government servant, he is entitled for reimbursement of the medical expenses.
Therefore, the Tribunal has erred in granting compensation in a sum of Rs.1,56,675/- under the head 'Medical Expenses'.
While granting the compensation under the head 'Medical expenses', the Tribunal has not deducted the advance payment made and prays to allow the appeal and reduce the compensation proportionately.

i) New India Assurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Satish Chandra Sharma and another1 (Satish's case)
ii) L.Eshwar Vs. Arijith Mandal and another2 (L.Eshwar's case)

sentences.text: On the other hand, the petitioner has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the compensation awarded is inadequate.

Having regard to the nature of the injury suffered,
period of treatment and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability, the compensation granted is on the lower side.

While PW-2 Doctor Ravikanth Kulkarni has assessed the disability at 43.6% of the whole body, the Tribunal has erred in considering it at 14% and consequently,
compensation 2022 ACJ 1211 2022 ACJ 784 granted in a sum of Rs.3,26,391/- under the head 'loss of future income' is on the lower side and requires reconsideration.
The compensation granted under the remaining heads is also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation.

15. Heard the arguments and perused the record.
16.
Thus, the impugned judgment and award is challenged by both petitioner as well as Respondent No.2- Insurance Company.

While petitioner claim that the compensation granted is on the lower side and requires enhancement, respondent No.2 has specifically pleaded that since petitioner was a government employee, on account of the injuries suffered he has not sustained any loss of income.

The voluntary retirement taken by him is not on account of the injuries sustained, but it was planned even before the accident and as such, he is not entitled for any compensation under the head 'loss of future income'.

Respondent No.2 has also challenged the impugned judgment and award with regard to grant of compensation under the head 'Medical Expenses' on the ground that petitioner is entitled for reimbursement and therefore, a sum of Rs.1,54,675/- ought not to have been granted.
In the light of the specific grounds urged by both parties, it is necessary to examine the impugned judgment and award.

17. At the outset, it is relevant to note that in respect of the accident in question, complaint came to be lodged by one Chandrappa, inmate of the Tum Tum alleging that accident was caused due to the rash or negligence of both petitioner as well as the driver of the Tum Tum.
However, while filing the charge sheet, the name of petitioner was given up i.e., petitioner was non-charge sheeted.

Admittedly, neither Respondent No.2 nor the driver of the Tum Tum have challenged the charge sheet alleging that either petitioner should also be added as accused or the entire charge sheet ought to have been filed against the petitioner.
In the absence of the same, the charge sheet prima facie makes out a case against the driver of the Tum Tum.
Therefore, finding of the Tribunal to that extent need not be interfered with.
18. In the petition, petitioner has claimed that he was aged 48 years at the time of accident.
However, based on medical records, the Tribunal has taken his age as 46 years.

Since, petitioner Bajirao S/O Manikappa vs Sanjeevkumar And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145423741/
5 claims that he was 48 years old, his age ought to have been taken as 48 years.
Anyhow, for the age group of 46- 50, the multiplier is 13 and it does not make any difference whether his age is taken as 46 or 48 years.
19. Medical Expenses:
Based on the medical bills, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,54,675/-.

Even though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 argued that while considering the medical bills, the advance payment is not deducted from the final bill, however, the learned counsel has not pointed out the specific bills pertaining to the advance amount to show that double calculations have been made.

It is also argued by the learned counsel for Respondent no.2 that petitioner is entitled for medical reimbursement and as such, he ought not to have been granted any compensation under the head 'Medical Expenses'.
Admittedly, all the original medical bills are produced before the Tribunal.
Therefore, it goes without saying that petitioner has not claimed any medical reimbursement.
Unless and until he claims Medical Reimbursement, he cannot be denied grant of the compensation under the head 'Medical Expenses'.

Therefore, the contention of respondent No.2 that he ought not have been granted compensation under the 'Medical Expenses'
cannot be accepted.
20. Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the evidence of PW-2, petitioner has sustained fracture of upper third of right tibia and lower third of right femur.
Though he is not a treated doctor, his evidence is corroborated by Ex.P-6 Wound Certificate.
Having regard to the fact that he had suffered two fractures, in all probabilities, it would be reasonable to expect that he was under treatment for at least three months.
However, the Tribunal has not granted any compensation under this head on the ground that he has drawn salary for the entire period of three months.

Having regard to the fact that he had suffered two major fractures, it would be reasonable to expect that he was on leave for three months and for having lost three months leave, petitioner is entitled for compensation in the form of salary for three months.
As per Ex.P-5, he was drawing salary in a total sum of Rs.42,661/-.

At this rate, for a period of three months, petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.1,27,983/- towards 'loss of income during laid of period'.
21.
Towards diet and attendance charges: The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.12,000/- under the head 'diet and attendance charges' which appears to be on the lower side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
22. Loss of future earning capacity:
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.3,26,391/- under the head 'loss of future earning capacity'.
It is to be remembered that at the time of accident, petitioner was working in CRPF.
Even after the accident, for a total period of two years he continued in service.
However, he took voluntary retirement as per Ex.P-13, which is the office order permitting him to take voluntary retirement.

This document clearly indicate that he had given application for voluntary retirement on 11.08.2016 whereas, the accident took place on 23.08.2016 i.e., subsequent to he giving the application seeking voluntary retirement.
23. It is not the case of the petitioner that after the accident, either he was demoted or given compulsory retirement on account of sustaining accidental injuries.
Therefore, the Tribunal has erred in granting compensation under the head 'loss of future earning capacity'.

Since, the petitioner Bajirao S/O Manikappa vs Sanjeevkumar And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145423741/
6 had already given application for voluntary retirement, it was accepted and he was relieved from service.
After the accident, he has not chosen to withdraw the said application seeking voluntary retirement.

To take advantage of the fact that in the accident he suffered grievous injury resulting in permanent partial disability, petitioner is contending that on account of accident, he took voluntary retirement.
If petitioner was compulsorily retired on account of having suffered injuries on the ground that he was not able to discharge his duty, things would have been different.

24. In L Eshwar's case, the Division Bench of this Court held that where the injury suffered in the motor vehicle accident did not affect the earning capacity of the injured, he is not entitled for any compensation under the head 'loss of future earnings'.

Similarly, in Satish Chandra Sharma's case,
the Hon'ble Supreme Court reduced the compensation enhanced by the High Court on the ground that the accidental injury did not affect the earning capacity of the injured.

Thus from the above discussion, I hold that petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head 'loss of future earning capacity' and the same is disallowed.
25. Pain and suffering and loss of amenities:
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.45,000/- under the head 'pain and suffering' and Rs.20,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities'.

Looking to the nature of the injuries suffered and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability, this Court is of the considered opinion that the compensation granted under the head 'pain and suffering' be enhanced to Rs.50,000/- and under the head 'loss of amenities' be enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
26.
Thus, in all, petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.3,82,658/- as against Rs.5,58,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
Of course, he is entitled for the interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

ORDER
( i) MFA No. 200477/2020 filed by the petitioner is rejected.
(ii) MFA No.202449/2019 filed by respondent No.2 is allowed.
(iii) The compensation granted in favour of petitioner is reduced to Rs.3,82,658/-.

The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the same with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization (minus the amount already paid/deposited) within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) Claimant/appellant is not entitled for interest for the delay of 76 days in filing the appeal.
